title: Apply the finding one step forward
subtitle: Inferences · 14 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **14 of the official questions in Inferences are this one** — 2 Easy, 6 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- It states one research result, usually that something affects one group and not another, or that A causes B.
- The blank then asks what would 'potentially' or 'likely' happen if a condition changed.
- The four choices are near-copies of each other that swap increase/decrease and which group is affected.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write the finding as a single arrow: condition → effect → which group.
- 2) Apply the change the question names to that arrow, including its direction.
- 3) Choose the option that gets both the direction and the group right, and cross off its mirror-image choices.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick the choice with the right direction but the wrong group, or the right group but the opposite direction.
These questions are built from swapped pairs, and a quick read lets that swap past you.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You pick the choice with the right direction but the wrong group, or the right group but the opposite direction.
These questions are built from swapped pairs, and a quick read lets that swap past you.
